'''Jaxson Reed Hayes''' (born May 23, 2000) is an American-Slovenian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]].

==Early life==
Hayes attended [[Moeller High School]] in [[Cincinnati]], Ohio.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.myrtlebeachonline.com/sports/high-school/beach-ball-classic/article191728964.html|title=Beach Ball Notebook: Moeller's Jaxson Hayes quickly growing into newfound stardom|website=myrtlebeachonline}}</ref> He grew from {{Convert|6|ft|2|spell=in}} as a freshman to {{Height|ft=6|in=11}} as a senior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.themonitor.com/2018/12/19/texas-freshman-jaxson-hayes-rising-hoops-star/|title=Texas freshman Jaxson Hayes is rising hoops star|agency=Associated Press|date=December 19, 2018}}</ref> In 2018 he took part in the Junior International Tournament (JIT), in [[Lissone]], Italy, leading Team Ohio to the win of its fifth title.<ref>{{Cite web|title=La Strada per l'Olimpo|url=http://jitlissone.it/it/la-strada-per-l-olimpo.html|access-date=2020-10-20|website=jitlissone.it|archive-date=October 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021132013/http://jitlissone.it/it/la-strada-per-l-olimpo.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 12 points, seven rebounds and four blocks per game. He committed to the [[University of Texas]] to play college basketball.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/ohio-high-school-sports/moeller-basketball-standout-jaxson-hayes-announces-college-decision|title=Moeller basketball star announces college choice|date=September 29, 2017|website=WCPO}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2017/09/29/and-winner-moellers-hayes-texas/718011001/|title=And the winner for Moeller's Hayes is Texas|website=Cincinnati.com}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at Texas, Hayes averaged 10.0 points and 5.0 rebounds per game while shooting 72.8% from the field. He scored a career-high 19 points along with seven boards, two steals and a block in a 69–56 loss to [[2018–19 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]]. Hayes injured his left knee in a loss to [[2018–19 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] in the [[2019 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]]. He was named [[Big 12]] Freshman of the Year. On April 11, 2019, Hayes declared for the NBA draft, forfeiting his remaining three years of eligibility.<ref>{{cite news |last=Caron |first=Emily |title=Texas Forward Jaxson Hayes Declares for 2019 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2019/03/28/texas-jaxson-hayes-declares-nba-draft |access-date=June 25, 2019 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=April 18, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== New Orleans Pelicans (2019–2023) ===
On June 20, 2019, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] selected Hayes with the eighth overall pick of the [[2019 NBA draft]] and then had his draft rights traded, along with the draft rights to [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]] and [[Didi Louzada]], plus a heavily protected 2020 first-round pick, to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[De'Andre Hunter]] and [[Solomon Hill (basketball)|Solomon Hill]]. The trade was officially completed on July 7.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-rights-alexander-walker-hayes-silva|title=Pelicans acquire rights to Alexander-Walker, Hayes, Silva|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2019}}</ref>

Hayes made his NBA debut for the Pelicans on October 10, 2019, scoring 19 points on 8-of-11 shooting against the [[2019–20 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] in an 11-point loss.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160689|title=Warriors vs. Pelicans - Game Recap - October 29, 2019 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-11-20}}</ref> On November 17, he made his first career start in place of the injured [[Derrick Favors]], achieving his first [[Double-double (basketball)|double-double]] with 10 points and 10 rebounds along with 3 blocks in a 108–100 victory over the Golden State Warriors.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160829|title=Warriors vs. Pelicans - Game Recap - November 18, 2019 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-11-20}}</ref> On January 9, 2020, Hayes recorded his second NBA double-double, scoring 14 points and adding 12 rebounds to go along with 4 blocks in under 24 minutes of play.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401161202|title=Bulls vs. Pelicans - Box Score - January 8, 2020 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2020-01-09}}</ref> Days later, Hayes recorded 18 points and 10 rebounds in a victory over the [[2019–20 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]], tallying consecutive double-doubles for the first time in his NBA career.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401161211|title=Pelicans vs. Knicks - Box Score - January 10, 2020 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2020-01-12}}</ref> The following night, Hayes posted a then-career-high 20 points in a 35-point loss to the [[2019–20 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401161220|title=Pelicans vs. Celtics - Box Score - January 11, 2020 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2020-01-12}}</ref>

On May 7, 2021, Hayes scored a season-high 19 points in a 107–109 loss to the [[2020–21 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gelston |first=Dan |date=May 8, 2021 |title=New Orleans Pelicans vs Philadelphia 76ers May 7, 2021 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022001003 |access-date=February 19, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> On May 14, he matched this total in a 122–125 loss to the [[2020–21 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCauley |first=Janie |date=May 15, 2021 |title=New Orleans Pelicans vs Golden State Warriors May 14, 2021 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022001059 |access-date=February 19, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref>

Hayes saw minimal playing time to start the 2021–22 season. On December 6, 2021, the Pelicans assigned him to their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Birmingham Squadron]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pelicans' Jaxson Hayes: Assigned to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pelicans-jaxson-hayes-assigned-to-g-league/ |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> He was recalled from the G League two days later.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 8, 2021 |title=New Orleans Pelicans recall Jaxson Hayes and Trey Murphy III, transfer Jose Alvarado from Birmingham Squadron |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-recall-jaxson-hayes-and-trey-murphy-iii-transfer-jose-alvarado-birmingham |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref> On January 1, 2022, Hayes registered a season-high 23 points, alongside seven rebounds, in a 113–136 loss to the [[2021–22 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Megargee |first=Steve |date=January 2, 2022 |title=GIANNIS' TRIPLE-DOUBLE LEADS MILWAUKEE TO 6TH STRAIGHT WIN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/nop-vs-mil-0022100539undefined |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He again scored 23 points, alongside twelve rebounds, on April 5, 2022, during a 123–109 win over the [[2021–22 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]] that helped the Pelicans clinch a [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]] spot.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wagaman |first=Michael |date=April 6, 2022 |title=PELICANS BEAT KINGS 123-109, CLINCH PLAY-IN SPOT IN WEST |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022101188 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> During the second half of the season, Hayes moved into the starting lineup and averaged 10.7 points and 5.7 rebounds per game over the last 23 games of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021-22 Pelicans Season in Review: Jaxson Hayes |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/jaxson-hayes-2021-22-pelicans-season-in-review |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref> The Pelicans qualified for their first playoff appearance since 2018 after play-in wins over the [[2021–22 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]] and [[2021–22 Los Angeles Clippers season|Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Finney |first=Peter Jr. |date=April 14, 2022 |title=CJ MCCOLLUM LEADS PELICANS PAST SPURS IN PLAY-IN GAME |url=https://www.nba.com/game/sas-vs-nop-0052100131 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Harris |first=Beth |date=April 16, 2022 |title=PELICANS EARN 105-101 WIN OVER CLIPPERS, CLAIM NO. 8 SEED |url=https://www.nba.com/game/nop-vs-lac-0052100211 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

The Pelicans faced the [[Phoenix Suns]] during the first round of the playoffs. On April 22, 2022, during a 111–114 game 3 loss, Hayes was ejected after receiving a [[Flagrant foul|flagrant 2 foul]] for pushing Suns forward [[Jae Crowder]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lopez |first=Andrew |date=April 22, 2022 |title=New Orleans Pelicans' Jaxson Hayes hit with flagrant 2 foul, ejected after shoving Phoenix Suns' Jae Crowder |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33788869 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Hayes finished the game with four points and six rebounds in only ten minutes of action.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Finney |first=Peter Jr. |date=April 23, 2022 |title=PAUL, AYTON HELP BOOKER-LESS SUNS BEAT PELICANS 114-111 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100143 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Pelicans wound up losing the series in six games.

=== Los Angeles Lakers (2023–2026) ===
On July 6, 2023, Hayes signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Jaxson Hayes |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-jaxson-hayes-070623 |access-date=February 8, 2024 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> He made 70 appearances for the team during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 4.3 points, 3.0 rebounds and 0.5 assist.

Hayes started 35 games in the [[2025 NBA season]] for the Lakers following the [[Anthony Davis]] trade to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Sources: Lakers to bring back Jaxson Hayes on one-year deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45661361 |access-date=October 23, 2025|website=ESPN.com|language=en|date=July 3, 2025|last=Charania|first=Shams|author-link=Shams Charania}}</ref> In 56 total appearances for the team during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], he averaged 6.8 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.0 assist.

On July 3, 2025, Hayes re-signed with Los Angeles on a one-year contract.<ref name=":1"/> Appearing in 66 games (including nine starts) for the Lakers during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], Hayes recorded averages of 7.5 points and 4.1 rebounds.

=== Utah Jazz (2026–present) ===
On July 10, 2026, Hayes signed a two-year, $12 million contract with the [[Utah Jazz]], with the second season being a team option.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2026 |title=Jazz, Jaxson Hayes agree to 2-year deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/jaxson-hayes-jazz-free-agency-2026 |access-date=July 10, 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hayes father, [[Jonathan Hayes]], played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and was the head coach of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]]'s [[St. Louis BattleHawks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Clark |first=Dave |date=November 2, 2018 |title=Fran Fraschilla: Jaxson Hayes is best long-term NBA prospect of more than 20 college teams |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2018/11/02/jaxson-hayes-fran-fraschilla-praises-texas-long-term-nba-prospect/1857833002/ |access-date=February 8, 2024 |website=Cincinnati.com}}</ref> His mother, Kristi (Kinne), played basketball at [[Drake Bulldogs women's basketball|Drake University]] (1991–95) and earned honorable mention [[Kodak]] All-American accolades and [[Missouri Valley Conference]] Player of the Year honors as a senior (1994–95). She recorded 3,406 career points during her four years (1987–91) at Jefferson-Scranton High School in [[Jefferson, Iowa]]. She previously served as an assistant women's basketball coach at [[Oklahoma Sooners women's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball|Iowa]] and [[Southern Illinois Salukis women's basketball|Southern Illinois–Carbondale]]. Hayes has three siblings: Jillian, who is in her fifth year as a starting forward at the [[University of Cincinnati]]; Jewett, a defensive end at the [[Virginia Cavaliers football|University of Virginia]]; and Jonah.

=== Domestic violence incident ===
Hayes was arrested on July 28, 2021, and resisted arrest by the [[Los Angeles Police Department]]. Officers were investigating a radio call that involved a domestic dispute between Hayes and his girlfriend. Hayes shoved an officer into a wall and was treated for minor injuries before being taken into custody.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 27, 2021 |title=Video shows police using stun gun on New Orleans Pelicans center Jaxson Hayes |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32099204 |access-date=February 8, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Hayes [[pleaded no contest]] to misdemeanor charges of [[false imprisonment]] and resisting an officer, and was sentenced to community service, one year of weekly domestic violence classes, and three years' probation. Hayes was not disciplined by the NBA, in apparent violation of league policy.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-11-08 |title=NBA never spoke with ex-girlfriend in Hayes case |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/42272088 |access-date=2025-03-17 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2024, [[TMZ]] published surveillance video of Hayes pushing his girlfriend, spitting at her, preventing her from exiting the house, and pulling her back through a doorway. On the video, his girlfriend can be heard saying, "I'm not going to let you hit me anymore. What the fuck do I look like, a punching bag?" After the video was released, the NBA reopened its investigation into Hayes' conduct.<ref name=":0"/>

=== International ===
In October 2025, Hayes announced he was pursuing a passport to play for [[Slovenia]], the home country of now-former teammate [[Luka Dončić]]. Dončić and Hayes share the same agent, who also represented [[Anthony Randolph]], a member of the Slovenian team that won [[EuroBasket 2017]]. The Slovenian national team allows for one naturalized citizen and Hayes cited the lack of open tryouts for the U.S. team as a reason.<ref>{{cite web | last=McMenamin | first=Dave | title=Lakers' Hayes pursuing passport to play for Slovenia with Doncic | website=ESPN.com | date=2025-10-19 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46653211| access-date=2026-07-29}}</ref>
